description.description:
This page allosw you to book reservations for overnight climbing permits in Zion National Park. Overnight climbing is defined as bivying overnight on a wall. Day climbs, as well as "fix and fire" climbs that take more than a day but do not include sleeping on a wall do not require permits. Bivying at the base or summit of a wall is not allowed.

Find Overnight Wilderness Permits, canyoneering permits, and Angels Landing hiking permits on separate pages starting from the Recreation.gov Zion gateway page.

Some climbing areas close every year beginning March 1 to protect raptors that nest on Zion's cliff faces. Please make sure to check the Seasonal Climbing Closures web page to confirm whether the route you prefer is open.

description.need_to_know_permit:
When planning your trip, please keep in mind:

  • Zion National Park's Climbing Regulations

  • This page allows you to book permit reservations for an overnight climbing bivy. It does not guarantee that the route will be open or accessible on your permit date(s). Climbing routes, trails, campsites, and even the entire park may close due to fires, floods, rock falls, or other reasons. 

  • Many climbing routes close during the year due to nesting birds on or near the route. Check the Seasonal Climbing Closure page for more information.

  • The park requires a Wilderness permit year-round for any overnight stay in the Zion Wilderness or on a climbing route. 

  • You may change your itinerary (subject to availability) in advance through your Recreation.gov user profile (“My Reservations”) or in person at a Zion Wilderness Permit Station. It is not possible to change your entry date. Increasing group size will incur additional fees.  

  • Permit reservation fees are non-refundable.

  • Wilderness camping and travel is subject to Wilderness regulations. All trip participants are responsible for knowing and obeying Wilderness permit conditions.

  • Your reservation confirmation email is not a Wilderness permit and cannot be used for Wilderness travel. Bring your reservation confirmation email and proof of identity to a Zion Wilderness Permit Station to pick up your permit.

  • You must pick up your permit in person during operating hours at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center Wilderness Desk the day before, or day of permit entry date.

description.season_information:
A permit is required for all overnight climbing bivys in Zion National Park. All persons who intend to sleep overnight, camp, or bivouac in the Wilderness, or who are in possession of equipment designed for overnight use in the backcountry, must obtain a Wilderness permit and prepare to present it to rangers or other park staff upon request.

  • To minimize impact, the park issues a limited number of Wilderness permits.  
  • One Wilderness permit allows for up to 14 consecutive nights of climbing Zion's big walls. 
  • The permit is valid only for the number of people, dates and locations indicated.  
  • Overnight bivy permits are required for all overnight climbs in the park, year round. Bivying at the base of a route is not allowed. 
  • Typical climbing season is March to May and September to November. Winter can be cold and wet, while summer is usually very hot. Zion climbing routes are all on sandstone. Please do not climb on wet sandstone, as the fragile rock is likely to break under pressure when wet.

description.need_to_know_email:
You have booked a reservation for a permit in the Zion Wilderness.

PLEASE NOTE THIS IS A RESERVATION CONFIRMATION, NOT A PERMIT.

  • ⚠️YOU MUST OBTAIN YOUR PERMIT IN PERSON AT THE ZION CANYON VISITOR CENTER THE DAY BEFORE, OR THE DAY OF YOUR TRIP.⚠️ 

  • Zion Canyon Visitor Center Wilderness Desk Hours of Operation: 8:00am-5:00pm every day. Allow at least 20 minutes for the permitting process.

  • Permits are not issued at the Kolob Canyons Visitor Center.

  • Zion Express Members: Please utilize your online account to obtain your permit.

  • If you are unable to use your reservation, or reduce your group size, please cancel or modify your reservation details in through your Recreation.gov account.

PLAN AND PREPARE

  • Group size maximum on Zion's Wilderness trails is 12 people. Groups may not split into multiple trips to the same trail on the same day to exceed this limit. Additional permit requests that would exceed the group limit will be denied or cancelled, and violators may be cited.

  • Guiding is not allowed in the Zion Wilderness.

  • Have a route description, any equipment needs, and the skills necessary to complete your trip.

  • Have a backup plan in case your plan changes unexpectedly. Carry a light source and extra supplies. Rescue is not a certainty.

  • Check weather and flash flood forecasts to evaluate risk. Consider possible trip adjustments to keep your group safe.

  • Have a means to carry out human waste and toilet paper. It's a requirement.

  • There is currently a toxic cyanobacteria bloom in the Virgin River and many streams in the park. Water filters do not filter out the cyanobacteria. Filter water from springs coming out of the ground, or bring your own water for your trip. Do not drink water from rivers or streams, even after filtering.

  • Food and scented items need to be stored in a bearproof canister.

Visit Zion's Wilderness Information and Permits webpage for more information.

For questions, you may contact a ranger by email to zion_park_information@nps.gov or by calling 435-772-0170.
description.need_to_know_order:
• Plan Ahead and Prepare

    • Know and follow Backpacking Regulations.

    • Self-reliance is key. Have the equipment and skills necessary to complete your trip.

    • Have a back-up plan.

  • Weather and Flash Flooding

    • Flash floods can quickly create deadly situations in narrow canyons. Do not enter narrow canyons if there is a chance of heavy rain in the forecast.

  • Cyanobacteria and Water Sources

    • The water in the creeks and rivers in Zion has toxic cyanobacteria in it. There is no method to reduce toxin levels from the water. Do not drink water from the creeks or rivers in Zion, even if filtering/treating the water.

    • The natural springs in Zion do not have the toxic cyanobacteria. Treat water for drinking from the springs by filtering, boiling, or using chemical treatment.

  • Group Size Limits and Guided Activities

    • The Zion Wilderness has a group size limit of 12 people. Additionally, a few specific areas have smaller group size limits.

    • A group is defined as any number of people sharing the same affiliation (family, friends, club, scout troop, etc...) traveling on the same trail or drainage on the same day. Permits will be denied, and violators will be cited if limits are exceeded.

    • Structured and/or formally guided activities facilitated by any educational, commercial, or like organizations are not authorized to take place in Zion Wilderness. Permits will be denied, and violators cited for such activities.

  • Leave No Trace

    • Packing out solid human waste is required. Burying or leaving behind poop or toilet paper in any way is not allowed.

    • Food and scented items need to be stored in a bearproof canister.

    • Natural objects and cultural artifacts must be left where they are found.

  • Overnight Camping

    • Campfires are prohibited in the Zion Wilderness.

    • Do not move rocks, logs, stumps, or anything else to build structures like tables or benches in your campsite.

    • Camp within the established footprint of the campsite.

description.quota_details:
Within Zion National Park, Wilderness camping is managed with quotas for designated sites and camping zones. The party size, length of stay, and number of people or parties allowed in a camping zone per night, have been calculated and regulated to provide for resource protection and visitor enjoyment.  

Individual parties consist of one to 12 people. Maximum group size in the Zion Wilderness is 12 people. A group is defined as any people that know each other, on the same trail or route, on the same day. Groups larger than twelve splitting into two smaller "groups" but still doing the same trail or route on the same day are not allowed.
description.season_information:
A permit is required for all Wilderness camping trips in Zion National Park. All persons who intend to sleep overnight, camp, or bivouac in the Wilderness, or who are in possession of equipment designed for overnight use in the backcountry, must obtain a Wilderness permit and have it with you.   

  • The park limits the number of Wilderness permits to reduce impacts.
  • One Wilderness permit allows up to 14 consecutive nights within Zion National Park's Wilderness. 
  • Half of all Wilderness campsites may be reserved in advance, online. 
  • The remaining sites are filled on a first-come, first-served basis in person at a Wilderness Permit Desk during Operating Hours, no more than one day before the trip begins.
  • The permit is valid only for the number of people, dates and locations shown on the permit.

description.cancellation_policy: Per person fees are refundable if the permit is cancelled or modified to a smaller group size before 5pm the day of the trip. The $20 permit fee is non-refundable in all circumstances.
description.description:
This page allows you to reserve opportunities for the "top-down" 16-mile overnight Virgin River Narrows hike. The Narrows is a winding hike in a river, descending down the narrowest part of the Wild and Scenic Virgin River. Hikers will need to wade and sometimes swim through sections of the river to complete the trip. In winter and spring, this hike is often inaccessible due to road conditions and impractical due to hiking conditions. Check the The Narrows webpage for more information about this often underestimated hike. 

Find other Overnight Wilderness Permits, canyoneering permits, Overnight Climbing (bivouac) permits, and Angels Landing permits on separate pages starting from the Recreation.gov Zion gateway page..
description.driving_directions:
The Zion Wilderness Permit Desk is located at The Zion Canyon Visitor Center, just inside the south entrance of Zion National Park, near the town of Springdale, UT. 

Driving directions to Zion National Park can be found here. 

The Narrows overnight backpacking trip begins at Chamberlain's Ranch, outside the park, and ends at the Temple of Sinawava, inside the park. The National Park does not provide any transportation to Chamberlain's Ranch. Chamberlain's Ranch is about a 1.5 hour drive from the Zion Canyon Visitor Center, half of it being on dirt roads. The road to Chamberlain's Ranch usually becomes impassable if there has been rain in the last 24-48 hours. Do not attempt to drive this road if there is snow present.

If you have two vehicles, shuttling yourself to the trailhead is possible, and allowed. If you only have one vehicle, your group will need to arrange for a private shuttle to take you and drop you off at Chamberlain's Ranch at the start of your trip. Arrange this transportation with one of the many shuttle companies located in the Zion area beforehad.
description.fee_policy:
Permit Fee: $20 per permit (non-refundable)

Per Person Fee: $7 per person per night (refundable)

The same fees are charged for first-come, first-served permits that are issued in person. This fee supports the permit and reservation management system.
description.need_to_know_email:
You have received a reservation for a trip in the Zion Wilderness. 

PLEASE NOTE YOUR RESERVATION IS NOT A PERMIT. 

  • ⚠️YOU MUST OBTAIN YOUR PERMIT IN PERSON AT THE ZION CANYON VISITOR CENTER THE DAY BEFORE, OR THE DAY OF YOUR TRIP.⚠️ 

  • Allow at least 20 minutes for the permitting process. Zion Canyon Visitor Center Wilderness Desk Hours of Operation: 8:00am-5:00pm. 

  • Permits are not available at the Kolob Canyons Visitor Center.

  • Zion Express Members: Please utilize your online account to obtain your permit. 

  • If you are unable to use your reservation, or have a reduction in your group size, please edit your reservation details in your Recreation.gov account.

  • Early notification of cancellations will provide others with opportunities. 

PLAN AND PREPARE

  • Maximum group size for the Virgin River Narrows is 12 people. Groups may not split into multiple trips to exceed the daily limit. Additional permit requests that would exceed the group limit will be denied or cancelled, and violators may be cited.

  • Have a route description, any equipment needs, and the skills necessary to complete your trip.

  • Have a backup plan in the event your plan changes unexpectedly. Carry a light source and extra supplies. Rescue is not a certainty.

  • Check weather and flash flood forecasts to evaluate risk. Consider possible trip adjustments to keep your group safe.

  • Have a means to carry out human waste and toilet paper. It's a requirement.

  • There is currently a toxic cyanobacteria bloom in the Virgin River, North Creek, and many streams in the park. Water filters do not filter out the cyanobacteria. Filter water from springs coming out of the ground, or bring your own water. Do not drink water from rivers or streams, even after filtering. 

Visit https://www.nps.gov/zion/planyourvisit/wilderness.htm for more information. 

For questions, you may contact a Wilderness Ranger at zion_park_information@nps.gov or via phone at 435-772-0170.
description.need_to_know_order:
• Plan Ahead and Prepare

    • Follow Backpacking Regulations.

    • Self-reliance is key. Have the equipment and skills necessary to complete your trip.

    • Have a back-up plan.

  • Weather and Flash Flooding

    • Flash floods can quickly create deadly situations in narrow canyons like the Narrows. Do not enter narrow canyons if there is a chance of heavy rain in the forecast.

    • The Narrows is closed when the National Weather Service issues a Flash Flood Warning, or if the flow of the river exceeds 120 CFS (3.4 CMS).

  • Cyanobacteria and Water Sources

    • The water in the creeks and rivers in Zion has toxic cyanobacteria in it. There is no method to reduce toxin levels from the water. Do not drink water from the creeks or rivers in Zion, even if filtering/treating the water.

    • Natural springs in Zion do not have the toxic cyanobacteria. Treat spring water for drinking by filtering, boiling, or using chemical treatment.

  • Group Size Limits and Guided Activities

    • The Zion Wilderness has a group size limit of 12 people. Additionally, a few specific areas have smaller group size limits.

    • A group is defined as any number of people sharing the same affiliation (family, friends, club, scout troop, etc...) traveling on the same trail or drainage on the same day. Permits will be denied, and violators will be cited if limits are exceeded.

    • Structured and/or formally guided activities facilitated by any educational, commercial, or like organizations are not authorized to take place in Zion Wilderness. Permits will be denied, and violators cited for such activities.

  • Leave No Trace

    • Packing out solid human waste is required. Burying or leaving behind poop or toilet paper in any way is not allowed.

    • Store food properly, do not feed animals.

    • Natural objects and cultural artifacts must be left where they are found.

  • Overnight Camping

    • Campfires are prohibited in the Zion Wilderness.

    • Do not move rocks, logs, stumps, or anything else to build structures like tables or benches in your campsite.

    • Camp within the established footprint of the campsite.
description.need_to_know_permit:
The Virgin River is closed to all hiking when the river flow is above 150 CFS (4CMS). The park closes the top-down route, including all overnight trips through the Narrows, when the river flow is above 120 CFS (3.4 CMS). The river and all canyons in the park close when the National Weather Service issues a Flash Flood Warning. Check the real time flow rate data before you go..

The road to Chamberlain's Ranch trailhead can become impassable when wet, often taking several days to dry after storms.

Spring Conditions

As the winter snow melts, the Virgin River often floods during the spring and the Narrows are closed due to dangerous conditions. The date at which the Narrows opens depends completely on winter snow levels and spring high temperatures. Visit The Narrows webpage and scroll to a table that shows the dates over the last 10 years when the Virgin River consistently exceeded 150 CFS due to snow melt. 

When the Narrows are open in the spring and the water temperatures are cold, most hikers require wetsuits or even drysuits to safely complete the hike while avoiding hypothermia. 

Summer Conditions

Early summer is usually a great time to hike in the Narrows, in later summer (July, August, and September) monsoon weather patterns may cause dangerous thunderstorms and flash floods. Weather is very difficult to forecast during this time of year. Flash floods are deadly, and visitors should avoid all narrow canyons, including the Narrows, when rain or thunderstorms are in the forecast. Visit Zion's Weather and Climate webpage.

Fall Conditions

Cold air and water temperatures in the fall usually lead to visitors needing wetsuits or even drysuits to safely complete the hike and avoid hypothermia. 

Winter Conditions

Cold, icy conditions usually occur all winter long in the Narrows. Drysuits are usually needed to avoid hypothermia in the Narrows. The road to the starting trailhead (Chamberlain's Ranch) is usually covered in a few feet of snow during the winter, making the hike inaccessible by vehicle. 

General Information

  • A Wilderness permit is required year-round for any overnight stay in the Zion Wilderness. 

  • Change your itinerary in advance (subject to availability) through your Recreation.gov user profile (“My Reservations”) or in person at a Zion Wilderness Permit Station. It is not possible to change your entry date. Increasing group size will incur additional fees.  

  • Reservation permit fees are non-refundable.

  • Wilderness camping and travel is subject to Wilderness regulations. All trip participants are responsible for knowing and obeying Wilderness permit conditions.

  • Your reservation confirmation email is not a the permit and cannot be used for Wilderness travel. Bring your reservation confirmation email and proof of identity to a Zion Wilderness Permit Station to pick up your Wilderness permit.

  • You must pick up your permit in person during operating hours at the Zion Canyon Visitor Center Wilderness Desk the day before, or day of permit entry date.
description.no_show_policy: Please cancel if you know you will not be able to go on your trip.
description.quota_details:
Within Zion National Park, Wilderness camping is managed with quotas for designated sites and camping zones. The party size, length of stay, and number of people or parties allowed in a camping zone per night, have been calculated and regulated to provide for resource protection and visitor enjoyment. 

Individual parties consist of one to 12 people. Maximum group size in the Zion Wilderness is 12 people. A group is defined as any people that know each other, on the same trail or route, on the same day. Groups larger than twelve splitting into two smaller "groups" but still doing the same trail or route on the same day are not allowed.
description.season_information:
A permit is required for all Wilderness camping trips in Zion National Park. All persons who intend to sleep overnight, camp, or bivouac in the Wilderness, or who are in possession of equipment designed for overnight use in the backcountry, must obtain a Wilderness permit and have it with them.  

  • The park limits the number of Wilderness permits to reduce impacts.
  • Narrows Overnight trips are limited to a maximum of one night per party.
  • Half of all Wilderness campsites may be reserved in advance, online.
  • The remaining sites are filled on a first-come, first-served basis in person at a Wilderness Permit Desk during Operating Hours, no more than one day before the date of the trip.
  • The permit is valid only for the number of people, dates and locations selected.
